explanations: The batcher is stopped and flushed before the HTTP server stops accepting and finishes in-flight requests. Requests still being read, or arriving on kept-alive connections while server.close waits, call batcher.add after the final flush; the timer is already cleared, so unless they reach maxBatch those impressions sit in memory and are lost at process.exit(0) while clients got 202. The server should be closed (in-flight requests completed) first, then batcher.stop().
The catch block sets this.buffer = rows.concat(this.buffer), putting failed rows ahead of anything added meanwhile. They aren't dropped, there is no immediate retry loop, and nothing exits.

Each flush is appended to the previous promise, so only one insert runs at a time and each picks up whatever is buffered when it starts. It is the opposite of parallel, it doesn't retry the prior batch (requeueing does that), and it has no notion of server idleness.

shutdown sets a 20 s timer that logs and calls process.exit(1); unref only means it won't by itself keep the loop alive, but pending I/O does, so it fires. The flush has no internal timeout, so it doesn't exit 0, and the hang path is bounded by the timer rather than SIGKILL.
